qa.name: Pronator Teres
qa.origin: Humeral head — medial epicondyle of the humerus; Ulnar head — coronoid process of the ulna
qa.insertion: Middle of the lateral surface of the radius
qa.function: Pronation of the forearm, weak flexion of the elbow
qa.blood_supply: Anterior ulnar recurrent artery, Radial artery
qa.clinical_note: The median nerve passes between its two heads — compression here causes pronator teres syndrome with forearm pain and weakness of median nerve distribution

qa.name: Flexor Carpi Radialis
qa.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus via the common flexor tendon
qa.insertion: Base of the second and third metacarpals
qa.function: Flexion and radial deviation of the wrist
qa.opposing_muscle: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus, Extensor Carpi Radialis Brevis
qa.clinical_note: Its tendon is used as a landmark for radial artery pulse — the radial artery lies just lateral to the FCR tendon at the wrist

qa.name: Palmaris Longus
qa.origin: Medial epicondyle of the humerus via the common flexor tendon
qa.function: Weak flexion of the wrist, tenses the palmar aponeurosis
qa.opposing_muscle: Extensor Carpi Radialis Longus, Extensor Carpi Ulnaris
qa.clinical_note: Absent in approximately 14 percent of the population — commonly harvested for tendon graft surgery; its tendon is visible at the wrist when the thumb and little finger are opposed

qa.name: Flexor Carpi Ulnaris
qa.origin: Humeral head — medial epicondyle via common flexor tendon; Ulnar head — olecranon and posterior border of the ulna
qa.insertion: Pisiform, hook of hamate, and base of fifth metacarpal
qa.function: Flexion and ulnar deviation of the wrist
qa.clinical_note: The only superficial forearm flexor innervated by the ulnar nerve — the ulnar nerve runs along its medial border and can be compressed at the elbow causing cubital tunnel syndrome

qa.name: Flexor Digitorum Superficialis
qa.origin: Humeroulnar head — medial epicondyle and coronoid process; Radial head — anterior oblique line of the radius
qa.insertion: Sides of the middle phalanges of the second through fifth digits
qa.function: Flexion of the proximal interphalangeal joints, flexion of the metacarpophalangeal joints, weak wrist flexion
qa.clinical_note: Inserts on the middle phalanx — distinguishes it from flexor digitorum profundus which inserts on the distal phalanx; tested by asking patient to flex one finger while others are held extended
